GTA welding between NiCr14-22Nb5-10 and In718 will be conducted using a NiCr-based alloy as filler material

Alloy ingots with nominal compositions of TiAl12-21Nb25-34, TiNi36-45Nb14-22, TiNi46-56Nb7-13 and NiCr14-22Nb5-10 were prepared by arc melting the mixtures of the pure elements in a Ti-gettered high purified Ar atmosphere.
the filler alloys were built up at the surface of the joined Ti3Al base alloy layer by layer in the sequence of TiAl12-21Nb25-34, TiNi36-45Nb14-22, TiNi46-56Nb7-13 and NiCr14-22Nb5-10

eutectic microstructure should be composed of B2-TiNi and bcc-(Nb, Ti)
the small-size grey phase labeled “4” is deduced to be TiNi3 compound
white precipitates (labeled “5”) primarily consist of Ni, Nb, Cr as well as Ti
the white crystals precipitated in layer “C” is presumed to contain both the Ni3(Nb, Ti) and (Nb, Ti)Cr2 phases
The average room-temperature tensile strength of the Ti3Al/In718 dissimilar joint reached 353 MPa
the strength value at 873 K was 245 MPa
in the Ti-Al-Nb zone, the microhardness (340 HV) exhibits a relatively lower value
the microhardness increases rapidly to 730~780 HV
The maximum microhardness value within the whole joint appears at the interface between Ti-Ni-Nb and Ni-Cr-Nb, which is 830~840 HV
the formation of (Nb, Ti) solid solution and Ti-Ni-Nb phase as well as Ti2Ni intermetallics in this region is the main reason for the high hardness value
mainly due to the formation of Ni3(Nb, Ti), (Nb, Ti)Cr2 and TiNi3 intermetallic compounds during welding
